Original /app/memory/GTEC_DIRECTIVE.md preserved (byte-identical to packaged copy, 12708 bytes) after test run via finally-block restore.
critical_code_review_comments: middleware_gtec_directive.py self-heal logic is correct: order (a) missing file → try packaged restore, (b) truncated file → try packaged restore then re-check length, (c) both unavailable → raise. Path resolution uses Path(__file__).resolve().parent which is stable across working directories.

_restore_directive_from_package() validates packaged copy length (>200 chars) before writing, preventing a bad packaged asset from silently ratifying a corrupted state. Ensures parent dir with mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) — safe in read-only containers only if /app/memory is writable at runtime, which is standard.

rca of the issue: Root cause: production Docker image did not include /app/memory (sandbox-only dir), so enforce_directive_on_boot() unconditionally raised RuntimeError, crashing container startup. Fix ships a canonical copy of the directive inside the backend package (/app/backend/assets/gtec_directive_canonical.md) which is always bundled, and adds _restore_directive_from_package() that writes the packaged copy to /app/memory/GTEC_DIRECTIVE.md on-demand. Boot logic now only fails hard if BOTH copies are unavailable — preserving the compliance gate while eliminating the false-positive prod crash.
